lines.text: Every great treaty in history was signed at a table. Ours was argued in a bath.
Oh. Oh, gods. Forty winters on that pass. My knees. My back. Why did nobody ever tell me about this?
The Old Bear purred. I hadn't known bears could purr.
Your bathhouse would make a fortune in Marrick, Lord Lucan. I want one. Before I sign anything.
So you're thinking of signing.
I'm thinking about everything. That's why I'm poor, and still alive.
Penhallow wouldn't get in the water. And he wouldn't take off his ring.
A family heirloom. It never leaves my hand.
Then the steam thickened around him, and the glass began to flicker. Like a candle in a draught.
And for a heartbeat, Penhallow flickered with it. He didn't look like a five at all. He looked like a very tired man.
The heat. I'm not used to it. Excuse me, my lords.
Tamsin was helping Tobin with the towels. She dropped all of them.
Seven rings around an eye. The steam showed it on the glass, like breath on a window.
That's the Order's mark, my lord. They stamp it on what they give their friends. I saw a whole case of those rings once, locked up in the College. Nobody would tell me what they were for.
So the third lord at your Moot is the Order's eyes.
And I couldn't stop thinking about that flicker. Rings don't flicker. You have five, or you don't.
Send him home, my lord. Tonight. Or let me walk him to the border, with my boot.
If we send him away, the Order sends someone we can't see. Let him stay. Let him watch. And we'll watch him watching.
I'll watch him, my lord. I'm very good at being underestimated.
Then be careful, Lucan. If he's watching you, he's watching me. And I am the one person in Greyhollow the Order still trusts.
Across the yard, Penhallow's candle burned until dawn.
